186: They were sitting and occupying themselves with Torah. In the meantime, the son of the innkeeper arrived and sat in front of them. He said to them, "That which is written, And that you will spare the lives of my father and mother, etc. (Joshua 2:13), and that which is written, so you shall give me a true sign [ot emet] (Joshua 2:12), what did she want from them?" Rabbi Abba said, "You have asked well, but if you have heard something, say it, my son." He said, "There is another question, as they gave her something she did not ask from them, as it is written, and tie this length of crimson cord to the window, etc. (Joshua 2:18).

Rather this is what I learned: She wanted a sign of life, as it is written, And that you will spare the lives of my father, etc.; and she said a sign of life is only found in a letter [ot] of truth. And what is it? That letter of truth is the letter, vav, since life is found in it (Zohar, Vayikra 2b). This is what I learned: She was requesting the sign of Moses. So why did they give her a length of crimson cord?

However they said, 'Moses has left the world. For the sun has set, and the time for the moon to govern has arrived. We have the sign of the moon to give to you.' And what is it? That length of crimson cord, as you say, Your lips are like a crimson cord (Song of Songs 4:3). 'The sign of Joshua will be with you, since it is the time for the moon's governance now.'" Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Yose arose and kissed him. They said, "You are certainly destined to be the head of an academy or a great man in Israel." And who was he? Rabbi Bon.
